gist.1: Home comforts set against the pull of the road, with a flash of the battlefield.
gist.7: Chorus: a soldier with his blood type and number on his sleeve asks to be wished luck, and to come back alive.
gist.12: He refuses victory at any price and would rather stay with her, but a star calls him on.

10: That I don't end up lying in this grass
That is: that he isn't killed here.
12: I could pay the price, but I don't want
Runs on into the next line: he does not want victory at any price.

gist.1: A winter city on cracked earth, two thousand years old, living under an ordinary star: the Sun.
gist.10: Two thousand years of war. Blood soaks into the ground, and within hours grass grows over it again.
gist.19: Fate favours those who live by their own laws and die young: they reach for the stars and fall, burnt by the Sun.

4: A city caught in the noose of its roads
13: Bitter joke: those who die young in war never grow old.
17: After three, it is alive again
Hours, not years: one hour, two, three, and the earth has healed over.
21: Those who live by different laws

gist.1: Far from home: a foreign sky, no familiar star, and no trace left of the roads he has walked.
gist.5: Chorus: with a pack of cigarettes in your pocket and a plane ticket out, today is not so bad.
gist.9: Nobody wants the blame or the dirty work, and without music there is no point even in going under.

6: Then things aren't so bad, as of today
9: And nobody wanted to take the blame for nothing
Idiom ‘guilty without guilt’: blamed though innocent. Nothing to do with wine.
10: And nobody wanted to do the dirty work
Idiom: to rake hot coals out with your own hands, for someone else's benefit.
11: And without music, even dying in company is no good
Twists the proverb ‘with people around, even death is fine’.

gist.1: He asks the cuckoo, the folk oracle of how long you have left, how many songs remain unwritten and what kind of life to choose.
gist.6: Chorus: he calls on the sun to look at him. His open palm has become a fist.
gist.10: Who will follow now? The strong and brave are dead, and few are left clear-headed and steady.
gist.14: Where has freedom gone? Life is good with it; without it there is only the whip.

11: The strong and the brave laid down their lives on the field, in battle
‘To lay down one's head’ means to die in battle.
14: Where are you now, sweet freedom?
A folk phrase for wide-open, boundless freedom, not ‘free will’.
19: Head and patient shoulders bowed beneath the lash

gist.1: A cold evening: glass instead of warmth, smoke instead of fire, a red sun burning out over the city.
gist.7: Chorus: our hearts, eyes, laughter, tears and pulse all demand change. We are waiting for change.
gist.11: A kitchen at night: electric light, cigarettes, tea, the blue gas flame. That is all there is; the rest is inside us.
gist.17: We are neither wise nor skilled, and don't need to be to understand each other. Yet suddenly we are afraid to change anything.

5: The day burns out with it

gist.1: Night falls over the rooftops. The city's lights are no match for the dark.
gist.5: Chorus: to those going to bed, sleep well. Good night.
gist.7: The moment he was waiting for: the silent speak up, and those with nothing left to wait for ride out, beyond catching.

3: The city fires a buckshot of lights into the night
6: Literally ‘a calm night’, the everyday Russian good-night wish.
9: Those with nothing left to wait for mount up

gist.1: An evening walk down an empty street: he smokes, she eats sweets. She wants the cinema, he suggests a bar.
gist.7: She chatters about school, a bad mark, a fight over her. He says nothing and they walk on.
gist.12: Her mother's lipstick, her sister's boots, dolls and balloons. She has to be home by ten.

9: You say someone got a black eye because of you
10: I keep a meaningful silence, and we walk on

note.7: A ‘troyak’ is a 3 out of 5, roughly a C.

gist.1: He writes her a letter: he can't stand what is on TV, he has no strength left, and he ignored the phone that wanted him up and running.
gist.9: Chorus: waiting for an answer, out of hope, and summer is nearly over.
gist.13: Rain for days, drinking with friends, a broken tape player. He is fine with the quiet.
gist.21: A building site outside, a restaurant shut for years, a tulip in a jar. Years pass like this, but maybe for a day or an hour luck will turn.

4: About how I nearly hit the bottle, but haven't forgotten you
7: But I told it where to go
‘Sent it’ is slang for telling someone, here the phone, to get lost.

note.26: The Russian Murphy's law: bread always lands butter side down.

gist.1: An ordinary sunny day and everyone is cheerful except you: no appetite, no interest, off to buy wine.
gist.9: Chorus: the sun shines and the grass grows, but none of it is any use when your girlfriend is ill.
gist.14: She is in bed with honey and aspirin, and you go to the party alone.

10: But you have no use for it
11: Nothing is right, nothing is as it should be

gist.1: A sleepless night in a place where he cannot sleep and does not want to live.
gist.7: Chorus: good morning, last hero, to you and everyone like you.
gist.11: He wanted to be alone and couldn't manage it. Dawn finds him at cards.
gist.15: Morning: the phone rings like an order to advance, and he goes where he doesn't want to go and nobody is waiting.

14: And you meet the dawn over a game of Durak
Durak (‘Fool’) is the most common Russian card game. He isn't acting the fool.

gist.1: Seeds in the ground beg for rain; inside him everything is on fire. Act now, soon it will be too late. If the key doesn't fit, break the door down.
gist.8: Chorus: Mama, we are all seriously ill. We have all gone mad.
gist.10: A clenched fist, a blow, poison in the veins instead of blood. A shattered world where some weep, some are silent and some are glad.
gist.16: You have to be strong, or why exist at all. Words count for little when it comes to blows, and still you hesitate on the shore.

13: A ruined world, bloodied heads, a loaf broken in two
18: You have to be strong, or else why exist at all
19: What will a thousand words be worth
20: When what counts is the strength of your arm?
21: And there you stand on the shore, thinking: to swim or not to swim?
A play on Hamlet: in Russian ‘to swim’ rhymes with ‘to be’.

gist.1: Everything arrived wrong: winter instead of summer, snow indoors, always waiting for tomorrow.
gist.8: Chorus: our eyes hold opposites, ‘forward!’ and ‘halt!’, the birth of day and the death of fire, starry night and lost paradise. So what do you want? Choose.
gist.16: Thirst without water, songs without words, sleep without dreams, and mourning clothes while the band plays a fanfare.

22: We wore mourning, and the band struck up a fanfare
A ‘tush’ is the short flourish a band plays to congratulate someone. Nothing to do with carcasses.

gist.1: They can't take risks: they have a home with the lights on. He doesn't know who is right. Rain waits for him, dinner for them.
gist.7: Chorus: close the door behind me, I'm leaving.
gist.8: If the cosy light ever bores you, there is room with us, and rain enough for everyone. Listen at the window and you will hear us laughing.

9: There will be room for you with us

gist.1: Show me anyone certain of tomorrow. Show me the dead of this road and the lone survivor of a regiment. Each of us has a part to play.
gist.5: Chorus: between Earth and Sky there is war, wherever you are, whatever you do.
gist.9: Somewhere people have an ordinary life: day and night, a son and a daughter, a world that adds up. But someone must be the wall, and someone the shoulder that shakes it.

4: But someone must be the door, someone the lock, and someone the key to that lock
The Russian word means both ‘lock’ and ‘castle’. Here it is the lock.

gist.1: He takes his assigned seat, cold, beside a neighbour he has never got to know. Everyone stares hopefully at the ceiling of a trolleybus heading east.
gist.8: Nobody knows why or where they are going. The neighbour wants to get off but doesn't know the way.
gist.15: No driver, a rusted engine, and still it moves. They hold their breath, watching where a star flashed for a split second.

8: All men are brothers, and we are the most distant of cousins
‘Seventh water on the kissel’ is the idiom for a relative so distant it hardly counts.
12: And so we wonder what use there could be
19: We say nothing, but we know what got us this far:

gist.1: A cheerful greeting to the boys and girls: watch me through the window, I'm planting aluminium cucumbers in a tarpaulin field.
gist.8: Three wise men keep telling him metal bears no fruit and it isn't worth the effort. He plants on.
gist.13: Pure wordplay from here: an angry white knee, buttons, clips and rivets, tractors dropping into a piggy bank.

4: And wave your little fingers at me, yeah
8: Chukotka is the far north-eastern tip of Russia.
11: The game isn't worth the candle, nor the result the work"

note.13: Deliberate nonsense, chosen for its sound: the Russian is a tongue-twister.

gist.1: They slip out once every window has gone dark. The last tram has left and taxis cost money, so they just walk.
gist.7: Chorus: we saw the night, walked all night until morning.
gist.8: Phone home so nobody waits up, take off your shoes. Cigarettes, matches and a bottle of wine will help them wait out the night, alone together.

6: The tape in our cassette player has run out. Rewind it
8: Step into a phone box and tell them to lock the door
Runs on: the door of your flat. She is letting home know she won't be back tonight.
13: It will help us believe that everyone's asleep and it's just the two of us here

gist.1: She walks past with someone else without noticing him. He holds his breath.
gist.6: In the evening he stands under her window while she waters her flowers, burning until dark.
gist.10: Teach me everything you know, make my dreams come true. I can't wait any longer.

gist.1: A big city on cold ground: streetlights, traffic, and above it a blood-red moon.
gist.5: Chorus: the house stands, the light is on, the view is wide. So where has this sorrow come from?
gist.8: Alive, healthy, nothing to complain about. All around is a ‘bliss’ in which you can't see a thing. Everyone cheers and runs forward as a new day rises.

4: And tonight the moon is red as a drop of blood
9: And, it seems, there is nothing to grieve over
Saying: ‘to live and not grieve’, a carefree life.

note.10: Sarcastic rhyme in Russian: ‘blagodat’ (bliss) with ‘ne vidat’ (can't see).

gist.1: Everything at home says stay: the coat on its nail, the scarf in the sleeve, gloves whispering ‘wait till morning’.
gist.6: Chorus: a strange knocking calls him to the road, his heart or the door. On the threshold he will say one word: believe.
gist.10: The station again, the sleeper train, no sleep, and through the clatter of the wheels he hears ‘farewell’.

1: Wires for strings, current through the hands
2: The telephone, in every voice, says: “Bye!” It's time…
7: Maybe my heart, maybe a knock at the door
11: And again the attendant hands out bedding and tea
On Russian sleeper trains a carriage attendant brings bed linen and tea.

gist.1: Time to leave again: his train has waited too long, and the wind and autumn, his sister, are at the door.
gist.5: Chorus: after the red-and-yellow days winter will come and go. Don't be sad. He will come home, victorious or carried, rich or poor, but as soon as he can.
gist.13: Tell me of those worn out by the street's dramas and of the temple of broken hearts. He dreamt that love and dreams rule the world, and woke to trouble.

1: My train has stood too long in the depot
7: ‘Woe from Wit’ is Griboyedov's classic play: the trouble that comes from thinking too much. Said here tenderly.
11: In silver, or maybe in rags
20: I woke up and understood: trouble

note.10: The Spartan farewell: come back with your shield (victorious) or on it (dead).

gist.1: Frost and ice everywhere. Snow falls like a wall all day, and behind that wall stands April.
gist.7: He will come bringing spring and scatter the clouds. In his eyes we will see sorrow; doors will open; and then we will see the light of the Sun.
gist.15: Wounded and weary, a star burning in his chest, April will die, be born again, and then come for good.

3: Only in my dream does the thaw drip and sing
‘Kapel’ is the dripping of melting snow, the Russian sound of spring.
8: And scatter the armies of grey cloud
12: Come, sit down, no sense in standing
Saying: ‘there is no truth in standing legs’, the usual way to offer someone a seat.

gist.1: A scream caught in the throat as the moment comes. Later, someone will long remember the fighters, unsteady on their feet, wiping their swords on the grass.
gist.9: Crows over the field. The sky laughed, then fell silent. The survivor's hand shook, and a moment became eternity.
gist.17: Sunset like a funeral pyre, stars watching like wolves. The dead lie with arms flung wide; the living sleep in a heap, without dreams.
gist.25: ‘Life’ is only a word: there is love and there is death. And who will sing if everyone sleeps? Death is worth living for; love is worth waiting for.

2: A scream is stuck like a lump in the throat
12: The sky: it laughed, then fell silent.

gist.1: We want to see further than the house across the street. We want to live, and we have come to claim our rights.
gist.5: Chorus: from here on, we are the ones who act.
gist.6: Born in cramped flats on new estates, grown up fighting for love. The clothes you made for us no longer fit.

2: We want to live. We are hard to kill, like cats
5: From here on, it is we who act!
6: We were born in the cramped flats of new housing estates
The mass-built apartment blocks on the edges of Soviet cities.
10: And so we have come to tell you that from here on…

gist.1: Late winter: grey snow, the moon in meltwater. They walk on, strong, striking matches with frozen fingers to light fires.
gist.6: Chorus: try to sing along with me. Stand up beside me.
gist.8: This is our day, read in the stars. We step onto an unfinished bridge, each shouting ‘I'm ready!’
gist.14: The weak drink and complain they were never allowed to sing. We keep walking.

9: Signs of fire and water, the gaze of the gods
16: They shout: You just try singing here!

gist.1: A list of things that almost work: a house without keys, a sun behind clouds, a word without letters, time but no strength to wait.
gist.9: Chorus: white days, white mountains, white ice. All he needs is a few words and room for a step forward.
gist.14: More of the same: a river without a bridge, a sail without wind, paints without canvas, a wound without a bandage, and an empty hand.

20: I have brothers, but no kin

gist.1: A new day, traffic back and forth. If the sun bothers to rise, so can we.
gist.5: Chorus: the anthill lives. One ant breaks a leg, never mind: it heals, or it doesn't.
gist.9: He dislikes lies but is tired of truth, looked for shelter and didn't find it. By the look of things the share of madmen is higher than they say.
gist.17: We could go to war against those who are against us… Our future is fog, our past now hell, now heaven. Anyway, it's morning. Get up.

3: If the sun can be bothered to get up
4: Then for us it's no big deal either
7: What you say to a child who has hurt themselves: it will mend long before you marry.
23: Our money won't fit in a pocket

gist.1: Today a goodbye, tomorrow a farewell for good. Someone comes home to ruins; someone falls from a crane.
gist.9: Tomorrow: an incurable diagnosis, a car, a surgeon's slip, a mine in the forest.
gist.15: The plane overhead tonight goes down tomorrow. Somewhere: war, epidemic, blizzard, black holes.

3: A wound in the heart will show red
The opposite of healing: the wound opens and reddens.
13: A young surgeon's hand will slip
16: Tomorrow it will fall into the ocean

gist.1: A place where nothing is what it seems: you can't tell a face from a snout, reward from punishment, gold from copper, or why anyone should sing here.
gist.9: Chorus: for the two of us, the sky for a roof and the forest for a wall, away from the fouled wells. That's the plan.
gist.14: Stones like soap, steel like tin, truth like flattery. He doesn't like what was here, or what is.
gist.22: A black night, water in the river, and trouble stops being trouble. Decide: here goes. Forgive me, and goodbye.

3: Here a pitchfork won't go into hay
11: The forest will be our solid wall
25: So, here goes, come what may. Forgive me, and goodbye
‘Byla ne byla’ is what you say before taking a leap: here goes nothing.

note.2: The Russian ‘carrot and stick’ is ‘gingerbread and whip’.
note.12: From the proverb ‘don't spit in the well, you may need to drink from it’.
note.18: From the proverb ‘you can't hide an awl in a sack’: the truth will out.

gist.1: Everything has its due: each star its patch of sky, each thief his chance, each dog its stick and bone, each wolf its teeth.
gist.9: Chorus: daylight again, and the day calls him out to fight, the whole world advancing on him.
gist.13: Where there is a flock there is a shepherd; where there is darkness there must be light.
gist.17: So: will you change this world, or accept it? Stand up and step out of line? The electric chair, or a throne?

19: Stand up and step out of line?
Literally ‘out of the row’: to break ranks, to be the exception.
20: Take a seat in the electric chair, or on a throne?
